claim_ledger.claim: The existing owned checkpoint module can store identity, expose control commands, and observe its diagnostic lifecycle.
The owned files can reject every ordinary route action while retaining formation, healing, consumable, status, diagnosis, trace, and checkpoint observation.
claim_ledger.evidence: Candidate admission is installed in BotWorldPopulationMgrUpdateBotKernelPreparation.cpp; ordinary route candidates are submitted in BotWorldPopulationMgrUpdateBotKernelFallback.cpp. Neither file is owned.

claim_ledger.claim: The owned files can prevent and count every route-generation mutation.
claim_ledger.evidence: ApplyValidationRouteManifestNode and MaybeAdvanceValidationRouteManifest mutate or admit route generation in BotWorldPopulationMgrValidationRouteRuntime.cpp, which is not owned.

claim_ledger.claim: The owned files can expose raid_runtime.controller_route_hold in normal status receipts.
claim_ledger.evidence: BuildRaidRuntimeJson serializes raid_runtime in BotWorldPopulationMgrRaidRuntime.cpp, which is not owned.

claim_ledger.claim: A start-held command can activate autonomy and install the hold before a later world update tick.
claim_ledger.evidence: Commands and StartAutonomyForCohort execute synchronously on the world thread; the checkpoint manager can reject reuse of an already-active attempt and bind the loaded profile immediately after start returns.

claim_ledger.claim: The existing checkpoint observation can be admitted as the only route path without touching the generic route candidate boundary.
claim_ledger.evidence: The diagnostic injection requires an active Route-owner path or armed route-hazard retry, both produced by the generic validation route candidates. An untyped allow-all tick would also admit unrelated offense and movement.

first_broken_edge.edge: controller route hold is absent before the first validation-kernel and route-generation transitions
first_broken_edge.consumed_mutation: route generation changes from 1 to 2 before arm acknowledgement
first_broken_edge.failure_postcondition: command_sent=false, checkpoint emission count zero, accepted checkpoint lifecycle count zero
first_broken_edge.correlation: cohort, attempt, server epoch, scenario, profile, route manifest sha256, generation, node, actor, fixture, seal, source commit

no_partial_edit.reason: A state-only or reporting-only hold in the original owned files would pass a helper test while leaving the production action and generation writers live. That repair is explicitly forbidden.

add_files.purpose: Add a typed controller-checkpoint-observation admission class instead of reusing formation or unknown semantics.
Install the attempt-scoped hold admission policy while preserving explicitly classified formation, friendly healing, bag consumables, offense suppression, and the one checkpoint observation path.
Tag the generic validation route action and movement pair as checkpoint observation only for the held actor and armed identity; do not add encounter, spec, raid-size, or difficulty conditions.
Call the shared hold transition before ApplyValidationRouteManifestNode and MaybeAdvanceValidationRouteManifest, reject/count held generation mutations, and permit them only after one valid release.
Serialize the required raid_runtime.controller_route_hold object in ordinary compact and full status receipts.

genericity_contract.naming_debt: Existing Chainwielder filenames may temporarily host the generic controller-route-hold primitive, but behavior and state transitions must be encounter-agnostic. A later rename is separate architecture work.

requirements: Compile and execute the exact generic hold transition methods used by production command, admission, and route-generation gates.
Fail-before evidence: an active unheld start admits a route candidate and generation advance before arm.

Pass-after evidence: held route action and generation advance are suppressed and counted; setup actions remain admitted; arm, terminal, and release each acknowledge once; route advance is admitted after release.
Negative cases: scope drift, active-attempt acquire, early release, duplicate acquire, arm, or release, stale or rejected lifecycle, identity mutation, and missing terminal.
Source-shape assertions may supplement but cannot replace the compiled transition fixture.

next_work_unit.return_to_controller: Only after the expanded production-boundary fixture is green and the generic primitive is committed.
